title: Use security models to reason about allowed information flow
summary: Security models state a protection goal and formal rules for information flow or state change. They help an architect distinguish confidentiality, integrity, and conflict-of-interest objectives rather than treating models as interchangeable labels.
outcome: Select the model objective that best explains a proposed access or information-flow rule.
managerMindset: Model names matter less than the property and flow rule they enforce. State the protected objective and then test whether the system’s rules actually preserve it.

sections.title: Models express different protection goals
sections.body: Bell-LaPadula focuses on confidentiality through rules such as no read up and no write down. Biba focuses on integrity through no read down and no write up. Clark-Wilson protects integrity through well-formed transactions and separation of duties. Brewer-Nash limits access that could create conflicts after a user accesses a competitor’s data. The star property describes a flow constraint in a model; it is not a substitute for context.
keyPoints: Confidentiality and integrity models can impose opposite-looking flow restrictions.
A model provides a reasoning tool, not an automatic application configuration.

sections.title: Map model rules to real enforcement
sections.body: A real system must translate a model’s goal into labels, roles, transactions, workflows, or policy decisions, then protect the enforcement mechanism itself. Consider exceptions, administrators, data transformation, replication, and audit evidence. A rule that exists only in design documentation does not preserve a property when the implementation or process permits a conflicting path.
keyPoints: Model enforcement includes administration and operational assurance.
Use separation of duties when integrity requires independent authorization and execution.

sections.title: Use security models as enforceable information-flow constraints
sections.body: Security models describe which subjects may read, write, or change information under a formal policy. Bell-LaPadula emphasizes confidentiality flow and label-based restrictions; Biba emphasizes integrity and avoiding contamination from lower-integrity sources; the Brewer-Nash or Chinese Wall concept restricts conflicting commercial information; and the Clark-Wilson integrity model uses well-formed transactions and separation of duties. Select a model by the protected property, classification or integrity labels, trusted subjects, transition rules, and enforcement mechanism. The failure is treating a model name as a complete architecture: an application, administrator, interface, exception, or data-export path can bypass its intended policy if enforcement and audit do not match the model.
keyPoints: State the protected property, boundary, decision owner, operating evidence, and residual failure mode.
Treat architecture controls as lifecycle commitments: configuration, monitoring, response, maintenance, and recovery determine whether the claim holds.

workedExamples.title: Financial release
workedExamples.situation: A payment release must be entered by one person and approved by another using controlled transactions.
workedExamples.reasoning: The main objective is integrity of the release process; a Clark-Wilson-style focus on well-formed transactions and separation of duties fits better than a confidentiality label model alone.
workedExamples.takeaway: Choose the model from the harm being controlled.

distinctions.difference: Bell-LaPadula prioritizes confidentiality flow; Biba prioritizes integrity flow and therefore reverses key read/write constraints.

misconceptions.claim: A security model by itself is a technical control.
misconceptions.correction: It is a formal or conceptual policy model that must be implemented, administered, and tested.

recallChecks.prompt: Which model is associated with no read up and no write down?

recallChecks.answer: Integrity through well-formed transactions and separation of duties.

scenarioSeeds.prompt: A researcher must not read lower-assurance unverified data before publishing an authoritative result. Which goal is being protected?
scenarioSeeds.decisiveDetail: The concern is contamination of trusted information, not unauthorized disclosure.

studyPlan.learn: State each model’s protected property before its rule.
studyPlan.connect: Connect model enforcement to D5 authorization and D7 audit evidence.
studyPlan.apply: Classify three scenarios as confidentiality, integrity, or conflict-of-interest problems.
studyPlan.revisit: In three days, contrast Bell-LaPadula and Biba without notes.
